description: Test your knowledge of MI7.1-5 | Respiratory Tract Infections.

cards.text: Which pathogen causes 80-90% of all URTIs, and what is the single most common cause of the common cold?
cards.answer: Viruses cause 80-90% of all URTIs. Rhinovirus (with >100 serotypes) is the single most common cause of the common cold.

tip.tip: Remember: 'Rhino' = nose = common cold; viruses dominate URTIs

cards.text: What are the four major virulence factors of Streptococcus pyogenes (GAS) and their functions?
cards.answer: M protein (anti-phagocytic, molecular mimicry), Streptolysin O & S (lysis of RBCs/leukocytes), Streptococcal pyrogenic exotoxins (superantigens causing scarlet fever), and tissue-spreading enzymes (hyaluronidase, streptokinase, DNase).

tip.tip: MESS = M protein, Exotoxins, Streptolysin, Spreading enzymes

cards.text: What is molecular mimicry in GAS pharyngitis and what is its clinical consequence?
cards.answer: M protein mimics cardiac myosin antigens, causing cross-reactive antibodies that attack the heart, leading to acute rheumatic fever (ARF) 2-4 weeks after infection.

tip.tip: Molecular mimicry = mistaken identity → heart damage; happens weeks later

cards.text: How is acute GAS pharyngitis diagnosed? List the key diagnostic methods.
cards.answer: Throat swab cultured on 5% sheep blood agar (β-hemolysis, catalase-negative, PYR-positive, bacitracin-sensitive). Rapid Strep Test (RADT) is fast with 95% specificity. Gram stain shows Gram-positive cocci in chains.

tip.tip: Bacitracin sensitivity = GAS; RADT is quick but negative result needs culture confirmation

cards.text: What is the morphological appearance of Corynebacterium diphtheriae on staining?
cards.answer: Gram-positive, pleomorphic rod arranged in 'Chinese letter' or cuneiform pattern. Albert stain shows blue-black metachromatic (volutin) granules in a yellowish-green bacillus.

tip.tip: Chinese letters + blue-black dots = C. diphtheriae; metachromatic = contains polyphosphate

cards.text: How does diphtheria exotoxin cause cell death? Which protein does it target?
cards.answer: The toxin's Fragment A catalyzes ADP-ribosylation of Elongation Factor-2 (EF-2), permanently inhibiting protein synthesis and causing cell death.

tip.tip: EF-2 → EF-DEAD; one ADP-ribosylation is enough to kill the cell

cards.text: Describe the diphtheria pseudomembrane and its systemic complications.
cards.answer: Grayish-white, tightly adherent membrane that bleeds on removal, forms over tonsils/pharynx/larynx. Systemic effects include myocarditis (heart), demyelination (palatal/ocular palsy, peripheral neuropathy), and adrenal damage.

tip.tip: Pseudo = fake; bleeds when removed; affects heart and nerves months after infection

cards.text: Which staining method best demonstrates metachromatic granules in Corynebacterium diphtheriae for rapid diagnostic identification?
cards.answer: Albert stain (also called Albert's methylene blue stain) is the best for demonstrating metachromatic (volutin) granules as diagnostic clue. Loeffler's serum slope culture enhances granule formation.

tip.tip: Albert's stain = Albert (the granule finder); tellurite medium = grey-black colonies
